title: Moderna takes RSV/hMPV vaccine back to clinic after earlier pediatric hold - AllSci

analysis.time: The trial started August 11, 2026, with primary completion expected in July 2027. The earlier pediatric program was paused in July 2024 after severe RSV infections in vaccinated infants.
analysis.location_and_population: The Phase I study plans to enroll 375 participants across Canada and the United Kingdom, targeting adults aged at least 60 who have previous natural exposure to RSV and exclude those who have received a licensed RSV vaccine or previously participated in an RSV or hMPV vaccine study.
analysis.event: Moderna has launched a Phase I study of mRNA-1365 (Profile 2), a bivalent mRNA vaccine targeting RSV and hMPV, in adults aged 60 and older. This follows a safety setback in a pediatric Phase I study in 2024, where severe RSV lower respiratory tract infections occurred more frequently among vaccine recipients than placebo.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Five of 35 vaccine recipients experienced severe or hospitalized RSV infections, compared with one of 18 placebo recipients. The US FDA's Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee recommended caution in further development of RSV vaccines in RSV-naive infants. The trial will provide safety and immunogenicity data through 2027.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The trial is ongoing, with safety and immunogenicity data expected through 2027. The US FDA has placed the pediatric program on clinical hold, but the adult program is proceeding. The study uses mRNA-1345 formulations as active comparators to assess the impact of the hMPV component on RSV immune response.

analysis.brief_en: Moderna has launched a Phase I study of mRNA-1365 (Profile 2), a bivalent mRNA vaccine targeting respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV), in adults aged 60 and older. This follows a safety setback in a pediatric Phase I study in 2024, where severe RSV lower respiratory tract infections occurred more frequently among vaccine recipients than placebo, prompting the US FDA to place the program on clinical hold. The new trial excludes RSV-naive infants and focuses on adults with prior natural exposure to RSV. It plans to enroll 375 participants across Canada and the United Kingdom, with primary completion expected in July 2027. The study will evaluate three dose levels of mRNA-1365 alongside two formulations of Moderna's RSV vaccine, mRNA-1345, as active comparators. The trial aims to provide safety and immunogenicity data, including direct comparisons between the bivalent candidate and the RSV-only formulations. The US FDA's Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee had previously recommended caution in further development of RSV vaccines in RSV-naive infants. Moderna faces competition in developing combined RSV/hMPV vaccines for older adults, with Clover Biopharmaceuticals testing a protein-based vaccine in Phase II. The findings from this trial will help assess whether adding the hMPV component affects the RSV immune response generated by Moderna's established RSV approach.
